title: Containers and application platforms

lessons.title: Containers: package once, run predictably
Choose the platform: registry, orchestrator, compute
ECS on EC2: manage the capacity beneath tasks
Fargate tasks: define resources, let AWS run them
Three ECS roles: separate host, startup and application access
Task definitions: configuration is part of the release
ECS traffic paths: bridge ports or task IPs
Container storage: match the data lifetime
ECS scaling: tasks and hosts are separate controls
ECS rolling deployments: calculate the safe window
Event-driven containers: launch work when it arrives
Queue workers: scale consumers and diagnose exits
ECS placement: filter first, then rank
Amazon ECR: publish a traceable image
Amazon EKS: Kubernetes control, AWS integration
EKS compute and storage: choose compatible building blocks
Elastic Beanstalk: deploy code onto a managed environment
Web and worker tiers: separate request and background work
Deployment policies: compare capacity, risk and rollback
Rolling updates: preserve enough serving capacity
Immutable deployments: replace a fleet after validation
Blue/green and traffic splitting: two release patterns
Beanstalk release workflow: package, deploy, observe
Configuration and retention: make environments reproducible
Clone, migrate, decouple: protect state during change
